findings.title: A same-key retry after OUTCOME_UNKNOWN does not survive a page reload for IntentForm creates and version upload
findings.evidence: IntentForm keeps the idempotency key in useState and the frozen payload in a ref (intent-form.tsx:62,69); UploadVersionForm keeps its key in useState (document-forms.tsx). After a reload or remount a new key is minted; the draft restores field values but not the attempt identity. Contract rev 12 section 0 guarantees reload survival only for bulk/import (server-memory slots). R9 handoff section 4 says a retry under a new key is disabled, which the client can only enforce while it still knows the attempt.
findings.impact: A receipted creation (for example create action or create document) whose answer was lost, followed by a reload and a re-submit, can create a duplicate: the backend dedupes by key only.
options: A: persist {key, frozen payload} next to the draft in sessionStorage (conflicts with the no-browser-persistence-of-legal-payload principle used for CL04)
B: extend the BFF session slot used by bulk/import to these commands (new server state; contract change)
C: accept and document as a local-profile limitation
findings.why_not_fixed: Needs a product/security decision and, for B, a contract revision. Not guessed.

findings.evidence: brief_replay.go:193-195 returns ErrBriefUnreconstructable unless revision is numeric, >= 1 and integral; TestReplayBrief_LegacyFilingRevisionUnavailable passes (missing key and "bad" value).

findings.title: Prior advisory F2: encode matterId consistently
findings.evidence: Probe P1: Next 16.4.2 passes route params percent-encoded (not decoded). Raw interpolation therefore reproduces the requested URL, and encodeURIComponent double-encodes any id containing %. For allowlisted ids ([A-Za-z0-9_-]) both are identical; any other id stops at pathId with not-found. No exploitable difference was found.
findings.note: MatterScope and history/page.tsx already encode and would double-encode only ids that cannot be valid. Adding more encoding would spread that inconsistency; none was added.

findings.title: document-forms.tsx calls fetch() for the version upload
findings.evidence: It posts to the same-origin BFF route (app/api/matters/.../versions), never to the backend, with a streamed binary body; the route validates ids with pathId and the session first. Deviates from "no fetch in components" only for a binary upload.
